status_note: active (turbo/pnpm monorepo; apps/www is a Next 15 + Tailwind v4 + fumadocs site that doubles as the shadcn-format registry host; 78 registry:ui items + 170 registry:example items; 1 open issue, AGENTS.md present for LLM contributors)
core_problem: Gives design-engineers ~80 copy-paste React/Tailwind 'marketing effect' components (shimmer buttons, marquees, bento grids, orbiting icons, globes, beams, text reveals) distributed through the shadcn registry protocol so `npx shadcn add @magicui/<name>` drops source into the consumer's repo instead of installing a package.
architecture: Monorepo (turbo, pnpm) with a single app `apps/www`. Components live as plain source files in `apps/www/registry/magicui/*.tsx` (78 files) and demos in `registry/example/*.tsx` (170). The registry manifest is hand-authored TypeScript: `registry/registry-ui.ts`, `registry-examples.ts`, `registry-lib.ts`, merged in `registry/index.ts` and validated with `registryIndexSchema` from `shadcn/schema` (Zod). Each item is a shadcn RegistryItem: `{name, type: 'registry:ui'|'registry:example'|'registry:lib'|'registry:style', title, description, dependencies (npm, with optional pins like 'cobe@^0.6.4'), registryDependencies (e.g. bento-grid -> ['button'] from shadcn's registry), files:[{path,type,target}], cssVars:{theme:{'animate-x': 'x 8s linear infinite'}}, css:{'@keyframes x': {...}}}`. The build script `apps/www/scripts/build-registry.mts` (1) runs `sync-example-registry-dependencies.mts`, a ts-morph pass that parses example files' imports of `@/registry/magicui/*` and rewrites `registryDependencies` in `registry-examples.ts` so the manifest can never drift from the code; (2) codegens `registry/__index__.tsx` (a `Record<string, {name,type,files,component: React.lazy(() => import(...))}>` used by the docs site's live previews); (3) writes `registry.json` and copies it to `public/r/registry.json`; (4) emits `public/llms.txt` and `public/llms-full.txt` (the full source of every component + examples concatenated, 660 kB) for LLM consumption; (5) shells out to `npx shadcn build registry.json --output public/r` which produces one `public/r/<name>.json` per item with `files[].content` inlined plus `cssVars`/`css`. `lib/registry.ts` serves items to the docs pages: it reads file content, strips `export default`, and rewrites `@/registry/.../(components|ui|hooks|lib)/x` imports into consumer alias paths via `fixImport`. Runtime deps: `motion` ^12.23 (32 of 78 UI components import `motion/react`), `cobe` (globe, WebGL), `canvas-confetti`, `rough-notation` (highlighter), `svg-dotted-map`, `react-tweet`, `shiki` (code-comparison), Radix icons/button. Tailwind v4 `@theme inline` in `styles/globals.css` declares `--animate-*` tokens and 22 `@keyframes` (gradient, meteor, marquee, marquee-vertical, spin-around, shimmer-slide, shiny-text, orbit, shine, ripple, rippling, rainbow, line-shadow, aurora, pulse, pulse-ripple, blink-cursor, background-position-spin, line, ping, accordion-*). No AI is wired in; AGENTS.md is a contributor prompt for coding agents (naming, hook deps, 'subsecond performance' aspiration) and llms-full.txt is the AI-facing distribution surface.
core_innovation: Nothing mechanically new: it is the shadcn registry protocol applied to animated marketing effects, with the one genuinely useful build-time idea being a ts-morph import scan that auto-syncs `registryDependencies` from real imports so the manifest cannot lie.
strengths: Registry item shape is a clean, Zod-validated (`shadcn/schema`) contract that separates npm `dependencies`, cross-registry `registryDependencies`, files with `target` paths, and CSS side-effects (`cssVars.theme` + `css['@keyframes ...']`) — exactly the granularity a section-variant `requires`/asset manifest needs.

`scripts/sync-example-registry-dependencies.mts` (ts-morph) derives dependency lists from actual import statements and fails CI (`registry-deps:check`) on drift — manifest-from-code, not code-from-manifest.

Roughly 20 of the 78 effects are pure CSS keyframes on `transform`/`background-position`/`opacity` with zero runtime JS: marquee, orbiting-circles, animated-gradient-text, animated-shiny-text, shimmer-button, shine-border, rainbow-button, pulsating-button, ripple, meteors (styles randomised once), aurora-text, line-shadow-text, neon-gradient-card, grid-pattern/hexagon-pattern/dot-pattern(static). These use `transform-gpu`, container-query units (`100cqw`, `@container-[size]`), and `offset-path` — compositor-friendly and portable to Astro with no island.

Consistent parameterisation via CSS custom properties set inline (`--duration`, `--gap`, `--radius`, `--spread`, `--shiny-width`, `--angle`) so the keyframes stay static and only per-instance vars change — the right pattern for token-driven design systems.
Emits `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt` from the same registry build, so the machine-readable catalogue and the human docs cannot diverge.
MIT, active (pushed 2026-09-20), 22k stars, lockstep with shadcn CLI 3.x and Tailwind v4 — low licensing and abandonment risk.

Some newer components show real engineering: `retro-grid.tsx` is a WebGL fragment shader with a CSS-keyframe fallback, DPR cap of 2, and a `prefers-reduced-motion` media rule; `floating-3d-particles` and `icon-cloud` poll `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')`.
weaknesses: Accessibility is not systemic: only 5 of 78 UI components (dia-text-reveal, floating-3d-particles, icon-cloud, retro-grid, scroll-based-velocity) reference `prefers-reduced-motion`; `styles/globals.css` has no global reduced-motion rule; infinite CSS animations (marquee, orbit, gradient, meteor, shimmer, shine, rainbow) run forever with no pause affordance (marquee only pauses on hover, opt-in). Fails WCAG 2.2.2 out of the box.

32 of 78 components hard-depend on `motion` (framer-motion successor, ^12.23). `motion/react` with `motion.div` + `AnimatePresence` + `useSpring` is ~35-45 kB gzip; a single BlurFade or NumberTicker island therefore costs a quarter of our 180 kB page budget and requires a React island in Astro. Blur-fade additionally animates `filter: blur()` which is not compositor-only.

12 components run their own `requestAnimationFrame` loops (particles, flickering-grid, glyph-matrix, icon-cloud, floating-3d-particles, hyper-text, morphing-text, cool-mode, retro-grid, smooth-cursor, pulsating-button, confetti); particles.tsx redraws N arcs per frame on a 2D canvas with a global `mousemove` listener that triggers React state updates per event — main-thread cost is unbounded and there is no IntersectionObserver gating on most of them, so off-screen sections keep burning frames.

globe.tsx: cobe WebGL at `devicePixelRatio: 2`, 16k map samples, `phi` advanced every frame forever, no visibility pause, no reduced-motion handling, no static poster. It alone would consume our '<=1 WebGL section' allowance and violate the poster-fallback rule.

Meteors, particles, dot-pattern(glow) and animated-grid-pattern use `Math.random()` in effects/render → non-deterministic output; breaks visual-regression snapshots and our 'everything computed deterministically' principle unless seeded.

Bento-grid is not a layout engine: it is `grid-cols-3 auto-rows-[22rem]` plus a card whose hover translates text 40px and reveals a CTA; the CTA is `opacity-0`/`hidden lg:flex` and only appears on hover on desktop → discoverability and keyboard-focus problem.

The library is the single largest source of what the public now recognises as AI-generated landing-page aesthetics (every v0/Lovable/Bolt default draws on it). Adopting its signature effects directly would undermine the positioning-driven design DNA we are building.

Everything is React 19 + Tailwind v4 + `cn()` from shadcn; class strings use Tailwind v4 arbitrary syntax (`inset-(--cut)`, `bg-size-[...]`, `mask-intersect`) that must be either kept in a Tailwind pipeline or hand-expanded to CSS for Astro.

AI-slop cliché signatures this library popularised — anti-slop tier-1 should BAN (in default/local_trust/premium positionings) or hard rate-limit (max 1 per site, challenger/leader only): shimmer-button, animated-gradient-text (orange→purple `#ffaa40/#9c40ff` default), animated-shiny-text badge ('✨ Introducing …' pill), marquee logo cloud (horizontal infinite), bento-grid feature section, orbiting-circles integration ring, border-beam / shine-border / neon-gradient-card glowing card borders, meteors, globe (cobe), particles / floating-3d-particles hero backgrounds, dot-pattern / grid-pattern / animated-grid-pattern / interactive-grid-pattern / flickering-grid / retro-grid / hexagon-pattern backgrounds with radial-mask fade, rainbow-button, aurora-text, light-rays, warp-background, ripple concentric circles, animated-beam 'integrations' diagrams, iphone/safari/android device mockups around screenshots, hero-video-dialog with blurred thumbnail, dock (macOS dock on a marketing site), typing-animation / word-rotate / morphing-text hero headlines, sparkles-text, text-reveal (scroll-driven opacity words), cool-mode/confetti on CTA click.

Still legitimately usable when constrained: number-ticker (counts once on in-view; must respect reduced-motion and render the final value server-side), blur-fade / text-animate 'blurIn' as a one-shot reveal (as CSS `@keyframes` + IntersectionObserver `class` toggle, not motion), CSS-only marquee for genuine content (testimonials, press quotes) with pause control and reduced-motion off, static (non-glow) dot/grid SVG pattern at very low contrast as texture, highlighter (rough-notation underline) for one word, scroll-progress bar, avatar-circles social-proof stack, progressive-blur on image edges, noise-texture as art-direction grain, animated-circular-progress-bar for a single stat, and pulsating-button only for a single live/status indicator.
patterns_to_steal: Registry item contract (`shadcn/schema` RegistryItem: name/type/dependencies/registryDependencies/files[{path,type,target}]/cssVars/css) → section library manifest: model each Section Variant/Arrangement as a registry-style item whose `css` field carries the exact keyframes it needs, so the Astro assembler only injects keyframes that the selected variants actually use (per-page CSS budget stays computable).

ts-morph import-scan → manifest sync (`scripts/sync-example-registry-dependencies.mts`, `--check` in CI) → build-time validator for our section library: derive each variant's `requires` for lib/components/islands from real imports of the .astro/.ts file and fail CI on drift, so `requires` is never hand-maintained.

CSS-custom-property parameterisation with static keyframes (`--duration`, `--gap`, `--radius`, `--shiny-width`, `--angle`, orbit uses `calc(var(--angle) * 1deg)`) → design_system motion tokens: keyframes live once in the design-system CSS; variants only set vars, which keeps the motion budget a static function of (variant, tokens).

Zero-JS keyframe ports: marquee (translateX(calc(-100% - var(--gap))) with N repeated tracks), orbit, shimmer-slide + spin-around (conic-gradient spark, `100cqw` container units), shiny-text (background-position sweep), meteor, shine/rainbow (background-position) → renderer: implement as `.astro` components with inline `<style>` + `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { animation: none }` and a `data-motion="decor"` attribute the motion-budget checker can count.

In-view one-shot reveal pattern (blur-fade/number-ticker use `useInView(once:true, margin:'-50px')`) → motion layer: a single ~600-byte IntersectionObserver script that toggles `[data-reveal]` classes, replacing framer-motion for entrance animations; number-ticker reimplemented with `requestAnimationFrame` + `Intl.NumberFormat` and SSR-rendered final value for no-JS/poster fallback.

llms-full.txt generated from the registry build → Decision Manifest / Gap Report tooling: emit one machine-readable catalogue of section variants (with `requires`, `signature_move`, motion cost) from the same build that produces the runtime library, so the model's eligible-set prompt is generated, never hand-written.

retro-grid.tsx WebGL-with-CSS-fallback structure (shader path, `MAX_DEVICE_PIXEL_RATIO=2`, injected fallback keyframes, reduced-motion media rule) → the template for our single allowed WebGL section: render poster/CSS fallback first, upgrade to WebGL only if `matchMedia` allows motion and the island is in view.
patterns_to_avoid: Adopting `motion` (framer-motion) as the animation runtime → 35-45 kB gzip per page for effects our budget says must be CSS; 32/78 components would pull it in; blur filters and spring-driven `offsetDistance` (border-beam) are JS-driven per frame and count against the 120 ms main-thread budget.

Canvas/rAF ambient backgrounds (particles, flickering-grid, glyph-matrix, floating-3d-particles, icon-cloud) → unbounded per-frame main-thread cost, global mousemove listeners, no in-view gating, `Math.random()` layouts; incompatible with static poster fallback and deterministic QA snapshots.

globe (cobe) as a hero decoration → uses the entire WebGL allowance for a decorative element with no content value, DPR 2 render every frame forever, no poster; only conceivable for a 'leader' positioning with real geographic claims from the FactRegistry, and even then must be poster-first.
Hover-only CTA reveal in bento-grid cards (`opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100`, `hidden lg:flex`) → hides primary links from keyboard and touch users; violates our a11y gate.

Shipping the library's default palette values (`#ffaa40` → `#9c40ff`, white shimmer on black) or its component names as-is → these are the literal n-gram/visual signatures the tier-3 self-cliché detector should catch; design systems must supply tokens, components must never carry colour defaults.
Copying the shadcn `React.lazy` `__index__.tsx` runtime and docs-site plumbing → irrelevant to an Astro renderer; only the manifest shape and build validation matter.

Treating llms-full.txt as an eligible-set prompt → it is a flat dump of 660 kB of source; our catalogue must be structured (Zod) and pre-filtered by eligibility predicates, never a raw corpus for the model to browse.
reusable_patterns: RegistryItemContract: a Zod-validated component manifest that lists npm deps, cross-registry deps, files with install targets, and CSS side-effects (theme vars + keyframes) as first-class fields.
ManifestFromImports: derive a component's dependency list at build time by AST-scanning its imports (ts-morph) and fail CI when the hand-written manifest disagrees.
VarParameterisedKeyframes: keep `@keyframes` static in the design-system stylesheet and parameterise per instance only through CSS custom properties set on the element.
OnceInViewReveal: IntersectionObserver with `once:true` and negative root margin toggles a class; the entrance animation itself is CSS; SSR renders the final state for no-JS.
ContainerUnitAnimation: use `100cqw`/`100cqh` container-query units inside keyframes so an effect scales with its host element without JS measurement (shimmer-button).
PosterFirstWebGL: render a CSS/static fallback by default, inject shader/WebGL only after checking reduced-motion, DPR cap, and visibility (retro-grid).
adoption_strategy: Adapt — narrowly. Do not add magicui or `motion` as dependencies. Port 6-8 CSS-keyframe effects (marquee, orbit, shimmer/shine sweep, shiny-text sweep, gradient text, meteor, reveal/blur-in, number-ticker) to zero-JS `.astro` components in the design-system layer with tokenised colours, mandatory `prefers-reduced-motion` rules, pause controls, and SSR final states, and register each with a motion cost so the assembler can sum against the 120 ms/180 kB budgets. Copy the registry-item manifest shape and the ts-morph import-sync validator for the section library's `requires` field. Feed the full effect list into the anti-slop tier-1 ban/rate-limit tables and add its default colour pairs and component idioms to the tier-3 cliché n-grams; whatever survives (number-ticker, one-shot blur-fade, content marquee, static low-contrast pattern texture, highlighter) is only permitted when a variant's `motion` budget and `design_compat` explicitly allow it.
